pageCache.text:
Welcome
A very warm welcome to Sunnyhill Primary School, a school where we pride ourselves on our inclusive ethos and ambitious curriculum set in the context of a spacious, historic site. We are a Local Authority school which has served Streatham since 1901. As a community school, we say Learning Together, We Will All Be Exceptional! With our 5 core values, the vision and values drive our practice and our approach to education. We truly live our values:
 Respect One Another Every Individual Matters Take Responsibility Strive for Excellence Try Your Best
Our curriculum reflects our locality and is enriched through educational visits to London and the south east as well as visitors into school. These support the taught curriculum and help bring it to life for the pupils. With a huge outdoor space, field and access to the Sunnyhill Nature Garden for forest school lessons, we ensure that our children are well supported with breadth as well as depth in the opportunities that they receive. We welcome parent/carer participation through regular events, both formal and informal for you to be part of your children’s learning.
We proudly hold the Primary Science Quality Mark in recognition of our commitment to STEM subjects and Artsmark Gold, reflecting our teaching of the arts. Our recent School of Sanctuary award and our work with the Anti-Bullying Alliance reflect our commitment to pupils’ safety and wellbeing and this can be seen every day through the wide range of pastoral support available at school. We pride ourselves on our strong relationships with parents/carers, working in partnership with you to ensure the best possible outcomes for our pupils.
We welcome you to visit for an informal tour which can be booked through the school office on info@sunnyhill.lambeth.sch.uk.
With warmest wishes, Head Teacher Sarah Wilson

At Sunnyhill, we have developed a high quality curriculum that has been carefully designed and sequenced in order to build up the children's knowledge and skills, as a result, expanding their long term memory.

pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club and After School Care
At Sunnyhill Primary School we offer extended day provision as an extension of the school day. Our team of staff are highly trained and we pride ourselves on providing an extremely high standard of care, keeping the children safe in a friendly environment.
It is an important term and condition of service that you collect your child(ren) on time. Late collection has an impact on children, club and school staff.
There is a late payment fee which must be paid the following day.
Payments must be made in advance via our online payment system.
Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club is open to all pupils from Nursery to Y6 from 7:30am until 8:45am, Monday to Friday.
We serve a hot breakfast consisting of eggs, beans & toast and cereal.
The cost of the Breakfast Club is £6.00 per day and Emergency booking requested on the day is £6.50 per day.
We offer a discounted rate for children from R-Y6 attending on a weekly basis of £5.50 per day/£27.50 per week and additional siblings will benefit from a further discounted price of £5.00 per day/£25.00 per week.
After School Care
Our After School Care is open from 3:15pm until 6:30pm, Monday to Friday.
On the last day of term when the school closes at 1.30pm, After School Club ends at 4.45pm.
The children are provided with a hot meal freshly prepared by our caterer.
The cost is currently £18.00 per day for pupils from Reception to Y6 and £18.50 per day for pupils in Nursery.
We offer a discounted rate for children from R-Y6 attending on a weekly basis of £16.00 per day/£80.00 per week and additional siblings will benefit from further discounted price of £14.50 per day/£72.50 per week.
The emergency booking requested on the day is £22.00.
There is a late collection fee of £10 per child for every 5 minutes if your child is not collected by 6.30pm.
Payments must be made in advance via our online payment system. We accept childcare vouchers and tax free childcare payments. Failure to make payment will result in your child(ren) being unable to attend afterschool care until payment has been made in full.

At Sunnyhill, it is our intent to develop responsible members of the community who have the tools to make positive choices in life.
From Reception to Year 6, we follow the ‘Jigsaw’ scheme of work to ensure that we meet all of the requirements of the National Curriculum and provide an approach to the teaching of PSHE and RSE which meets the needs of the diverse community that we share. Jigsaw brings together PSHE Education, compulsory Relationships and Health Education, emotional literacy, mindfulness, social skills and spiritual development. It is designed as a whole school approach, with all year groups working on the same theme (Puzzle) at the same time at their own level. Personal Development
What is personal development?
Personal development refers to the development of character, skills, attitudes, values, and behaviours which play a crucial role in shaping a child’s future success and well-being.
What does personal development look like at Sunnyhill?
Personal development is at the heart of our curriculum and we want pupils to leave Sunnyhill Primary School ready to take on the next chapter in their lives. As part of their personal development journey we want all children to experience:
Our vision is ‘Learning Together, We Will All Be Exceptional!’ With our 5 core values, the vision and values drive our practice and our approach to education. We truly live our values:
Through the children’s learning and extra curricular opportunities, we develop the character strengths of confidence, resilience, inspiration, motivation, courage, empathy and ambition. These character strengths underpin our school vision and dictate our values. We teach pupils how to develop their character strengths through real experiences, exposure to diverse role models and external speakers, and by giving them practical strategies they can apply to help them to navigate challenges. We believe that every interaction (and every lesson) is an opportunity to develop the good character of our pupils.
Character is primarily ‘caught’ (picked up through experiences), therefore we create an environment that nurtures these character strengths. Our expectations of behaviour are driven by our core values with class rewards, behaviour tickets and celebration assemblies motivating the children to develop self-control, empathy and a sense of responsibility.
Character is also ‘taught’ through assemblies and links made in learning across the curriculum.
Finally, our environment provides opportunities for character to be ‘sought’ through experiences during and outside the school day that broaden the pupils' passions and interests.

Mathematics
By the end of primary school, Sunnyhill pupils will be confident, competent and successful mathematicians who achieve fluency and have an ability to solve problems and think mathematically.
We expect our pupils to:
Work in a systematic way
Communicate confidently using mathematical language.
How Maths is taught at Sunnyhill:
At Sunnyhill, we use the White Rose Maths scheme from Year 1 to Year 6. White Rose is designed to give sufficient time for maths topics to be explored and concepts to be understood in depth. We use flashbacks which support children’s recall of previously learnt topics by revising something the children learned in the previous lesson, last week and last month or year.
In the early years and KS1, pupils develop fluency through a short daily session called Mastering Number. The programme aims to strengthen the understanding of number, and fluency with number facts, among children in Reception and Years 1 and 2.
From Year 1 to Year 6, all teachers using guided practice to secure a mathematical process at the start of the lesson, which is then applied to word problems. All pupils work from the same starting point with more complex problems applied according to pupils’ ability to access them. We do not stream or set pupils in maths - all pupils work together in mixed groups and access learning at their own pace.
Pupils gain understanding in stages, using ‘concrete’ resources such as counters, cubes, place value counters and diennes to represent numbers. They then use their own representations known as ‘pictorial’ to support understanding. When they no longer require this support, pupils will move into ‘abstract’ concepts, applying known facts and processes.
Outdoor learning: By taking learning and the classroom outside, it gives children opportunities to apply their learning in their natural environment - an approach we value at Sunnyhill.
Financial Education: At Sunnyhill, we teach pupils about financial education, focusing on the basics of money management: budgeting, saving, debt, investing, and giving. This is a particular focus of maths week.
Maths At Home: Pupils are given maths homework weekly. More information can be found in the homework policy here: Homework Policy
Below are some useful websites you may find useful when helping your child at home with maths:
Maths Dictionary for Parents: https://thirdspacelearning.com/blog/primary-maths-dictionary/
This A-Z online maths glossary includes some of the key words and phrases that your child will learn in school.

Volunteers
We value and appreciate the time our volunteers dedicate to support our school community to promote learning. We offer volunteering opportunities over a minimum of a full term.
Volunteers listen to children read, assist with school activities, help out at the library, accompany children on school trips and to swimming lessons.
Our children’s safety and wellbeing is very important and all volunteers are expected to complete a DBS check before starting at the school. If you have not been resident in the UK for the past 5 years you may also be asked to provide a certificate of good conduct from the country (or countries) where you resided. We will also request volunteers provide information and contact details of two referees who can comment on volunteer’s suitability to work with children.
Volunteers are required to sign a Volunteer Agreement, which sets out school’s expectations and read following important school policies:
If you volunteer in Nursery or Reception class you will be required to complete Childcare Disqualification Declaration Form.
We are always pleased to hear from potential volunteers.
If you are interested in becoming a volunteer at Sunnyhill Primary School, please email our Deputy Head Teacher for Inclusion, Nicola Gentleman at ngentleman@sunnyhill.lambeth.sch.uk .
Thank you for offering your time to help us in school!

Applications for a school place are made directly to the local authority in which you live.
Local Authority manages school 's admission and appeal process. If you wish to find out about the admission and appeal arrangements follow this link:
Reception Admissions:
Applications can be made from 1 September 2026 and the deadline to apply for Reception place is 15 January.
You will receive the outcome on the National Offer Day, 16th April 2027. You have to respond to the offer by 30th April 2027.
To apply please click on the link: Apply for a school place
Starting primary school in Lambeth 2027-28
In-Year School Admissions:
An in-year primary school application has to be completed if:
To apply please click on the link: Apply for a school place
Once you have applied for a school place, the waiting list is held and managed by Lambeth School Admissions Team. To speak to the Admissions Team or to find out where you are on the waiting list, please call 0207 926 9503, or email schooladmissions@lambeth.gov.uk.
Nursery Admissions:
Nursery Admissions are managed by the school.
We are currently offering 15x full time places and 40x part-time places: morning (8.45am-11.45am) or afternoon (12.15pm-3.15pm) sessions.
Working parents are entitled to 30hrs of government funded childcare a week.
To check if you are eligible for full time childcare please go to https://www.gov.uk/30-hours-free-childcare
If you are eligible, you’ll get a childcare account and a DERN code, which you have to provide on your application together with you National Insurance Number.
IMPORTANT: You must confirm your details every 3 months, otherwise your code will expire and you may lose your full time place.
Nursery Applications must be made directly to the school office and supporting documents confirming your child’s identity, date of birth and address must be provided. Incomplete forms won’t be processed.
Nursery Admissions Policy is available within the Policies section.
Secondary School Transition
The Secondary School application submission deadline is 31st October and parents/carers of pupils starting Year 6 in September need to apply for their child Secondary School place by that deadline.
Before applying to a Secondary School you are advised to:
Starting secondary school in Lambeth 2027-28
The London-wide application system means that wherever you live, you can apply for a secondary school place in up to six schools using one single form from your council. Lambeth residents are advised to apply online at eAdmissions or visit Lambeth Website for more information.
Once you have submitted your application you will be issued with a unique reference number similar to 208-2014-09-E-001234, which will be proof that your application has been received. The online system is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, from 1st September up until midnight on the 31st October. However, you are encouraged to submit your application no later than 23rd October, to allow sufficient time for checking. The National Offer Day is on 1st March 2027.
If you would like any additional information please contact the Lambeth School Admissions Team on: 0207 926 9503 or via schooladmissions@lambeth.gov.uk, or visit the eAdmissions website.
NB: If you live in a different borough to Lambeth, please apply using your home borough's Common Application Form, even if you are applying for a Lambeth school.
Supplementary Forms
Some secondary schools ask you to complete a Supplementary Information Form (SIF) or other additional form to provide extra information when you apply for a place. You must ensure that you complete these forms where needed and return them to the school/submit it by their deadline for the admissions criteria to be looked at fully.
Secondary school application support
We also hold a secondary transfer meeting on Monday, 7th September at 5pm for parents/carers of pupils in Y6 to explain the procedures and to provide support with the secondary school application process.

Languages (MFL)
With Spanish being our most spoken language by the children in our school, we use Primary Languages Network to equip the children with the knowledge to develop their language skills in Spanish.
At Sunnyhill, we believe that the learning of a language provides a valuable educational, social and cultural experience for all of our pupils. Our Spanish lessons help children to further develop their communication skills, including the core skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing.
We believe that learning another language gives children a new and broader perspective on the world, encouraging them to understand their own cultures and those of others.
Primary Languages Network is a live scheme which is continually updated and revised in order to meet current National Curriculum standards. There is staff training provided and lessons are supported by accompanying videos spoken by native speakers (to ensure accurate pronunciation), links to authentic literature, songs, games, cultural points of reference and seasonal events. Where possible, children will learn about other areas of the curriculum through Spanish e.g. Year 5 learn how to name the planets in Spanish and they also learn about the plants in Science.
For our native Spanish speakers we adapt the lessons so that those children can practise and refine their Spanish skills. They are also encouraged to volunteer as Junior Translators for those children who are new to English or visitors to our school and they support other children in lessons with their understanding of Spanish.
In EYFS and Key Stage 1, where the learning of languages is not compulsory, we lay the foundations for future learning through singing songs, reciting rhymes, greeting in Spanish, counting up to 10 and having items in the classroom environment labeled in Spanish.

Pupil Leaders
At Sunnyhill we believe that the children should be at the heart of everything we do. That starts with giving them a voice and enabling them to have a tangible impact on their environment.
Every child at Sunnyhill, from Nursery to Year 6, has the opportunity to have a say in their learning and environment by submitting sensible suggestions every long term, to our School council.
To ensure every child is heard, we have a member of staff dedicated to training, supporting and facilitating the pupil voice teams. Currently, a quarter of pupils are enrolled in a pupil leadership role.

Refill at Sunnyhill - February ‘26
On 26th February, the Green Team opened their first eco-refill shop ‘Refill at Sunnyhill’. They chose the name of their shop, decided on their products and came up with the business plan. They were really happy to serve their first customers and are looking forward to their next opening date in March.

Music
At Sunnyhill School, we include a vibrant music and creative arts offer both within and beyond our curriculum.
Through the Lambeth Music Programme, our pupils develop foundation skills in music through singing activities based on the Kodaly teaching method. In subsequent years, pupils further their musicianship by learning to play an instrument within a whole-class ensemble. Our pupils learn to read music to develop an understanding of a variety of music styles. Pupils will enjoy the many associated benefits of music through composing music, recitals and performances (both performing and watching).
From Nursery to Year 6, the pupils are given opportunities to perform in front of an audience. Such performances develop skills such as self-expression, confidence, risk-taking, cooperation and communication. Our pupils will experience the sense of achievement that the performing arts can bring.
